doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Growing up in Endicott and learning drums
title: Getting her first drums and joining the jazz band
summary: After Buddy Rich she pleaded for drums; her mother bought the wrong drum, and a teacher pushed her to try out for the high school jazz band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Yeah. But then when I saw Buddy, that was it.
And that’s when you kind of started on the whole drum set?

I actually pleaded with my mother to buy me a drum set which was like there is just no way, you know, my daughter is not playing the drums kind of attitude. But then after my pleading and screaming I remember she bought me a, I begged for a snare drum, which is the first drum you would get, and she came home and didn’t know a drum from anything, and went to the music store and the guy told her, “this is a snare drum.” And this was this big like funky weird brown tom-tom, and just the fact that she bought it for me, I’ve told her now but I could never tell her for years it was the wrong drum. So I’d be practicing on this tom-tom and then I finally got into drum set when I was in high school. I was terrified to try out for the jazz band and another good teacher actually said something like, “what are you stupid? Just go ahead.” Because there were no girls in it. No girls had ever played the drums anyway. So he was encouraging.
